player_benefit: Players can understand what is possible and how to begin without an external wiki or a quest toll gate.
adventure_route: Discovery may reveal optional possibilities and first milestones, but never withholds instructions for an expected process.
civic_route: A settlement noticeboard, mentor, or Field Journal turns local knowledge into visible next steps.
mastery_route: A breadth or technique milestone explains why a new capability matters instead of awarding an opaque level.
technical_route: Recipe viewing, machine descriptions, and bounded input/output summaries expose the process and its limits.
economic_route: A cartographer, trader, or steward can teach a documented process through a service or commission.
dependencies: Field Guide; recipe-viewer integration where recipes exist; Matcha adapter for audited tutorial behaviour.
existing_mod_candidate: Matcha tutorial and advancement tree; recipe viewer candidate TBD (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: unify explanations, discovery state, and third-party inputs behind stable concepts.
notes: Route columns map to Adventure, Builder/Civic, Artisan/Producer mastery, Engineer/Technical, and Merchant/Steward. All routes are additive to vanilla play.

player_benefit: A named tool or piece of equipment can be restored instead of becoming a disposable loss or an XP-farm obligation.
adventure_route: Field kits and salvage make an expedition survivable without providing free full repair everywhere.
civic_route: A registered workshop or smith restores full condition using visible materials, time, or service requirements.
mastery_route: Smithing evidence can improve service quality, but ordinary repair remains available without a specialist loadout.
technical_route: A bounded repair station may automate handling only when it consumes real inputs and validates the item transaction.
economic_route: A paid repair, commission, or imported part provides a solo route and a multiplayer service niche.
dependencies: Versioned equipment component; repair materials; workshop or service registration; atomic server transaction.
existing_mod_candidate: Vanilla anvil; Matcha endless_repairs is audit-dependent and not sufficient (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: own condition, repair precedence, migration, and safe failure.
notes: At least field and workshop repair must remain distinct. Matcha's repair-cost reset cannot be treated as proof of retained broken items.

player_benefit: Zero condition makes an item broken and unusable while preserving identity, history, and recoverable data.
adventure_route: A broken item remains recoverable after an expedition, death, or a difficult crossing.
civic_route: A home archive, repair bench, or heirloom register preserves the item's identity and history.
mastery_route: An item's learned path and craftsmanship record remain meaningful after breakage and repair.
technical_route: A server-authoritative damage boundary performs an idempotent broken transition rather than deleting the stack.
economic_route: A recovery or maintenance contract can protect a named item without creating a free replacement loop.
dependencies: Equipment schema version; item components; death, container, trade, restart, and migration handling.
existing_mod_candidate: No existing candidate verified; Forever equipment boundary is the design owner.
custom_integration_required: Yes: intercept condition transitions and preserve unknown components safely.
notes: This is a preservation rule, not a power bonus. No route may duplicate the item or its contents.

player_benefit: A small personal cache carries tools, food, maps, and emergency supplies before end-game storage is reached.
adventure_route: A cache can be found or its construction method learned during a meaningful expedition.
civic_route: A settlement outfitter, stable, or workshop can commission and expand a cache.
mastery_route: Explorer or Steward evidence can unlock a bounded expansion from nine to eighteen slots.
technical_route: Component validation enforces no nesting and prevents recursive inventory capacity.
economic_route: A merchant can sell a cache or its fittings without making another player mandatory.
dependencies: Traveler's Cache schema; no-container-nesting rule; item drop, death, trade, and restart semantics.
existing_mod_candidate: Traveler's Cache is custom design; backpack mod candidate TBD (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: cache component, nesting validation, and duplication-safe movement.
notes: Portable storage is convenience, not a replacement for warehouses. It must never contain another inventory-bearing item.

player_benefit: At a settlement, a player can locate physical stock by item, tag, condition, owner, or location without opening every container.
adventure_route: A discovered storehouse or outpost can reveal a local search service.
civic_route: A registered warehouse and its access permissions give a settlement a useful civic service.
mastery_route: Steward or Builder project evidence can improve facets and explainability, not grant magical access.
technical_route: An indexed, bounded query reads derived summaries while physical containers remain authoritative.
economic_route: A warehouse operator can charge for indexing or fulfilment while direct vanilla access remains free.
dependencies: Registered containers; rebuildable index; bounded queries; permissions; atomic stack transfers.
existing_mod_candidate: Storage-index mod candidate TBD (provisional); vanilla containers remain the source of truth.
custom_integration_required: Yes: physical handles, revisions, permission checks, and stale-result handling.
notes: Search visibility must identify where the stack is. It must not silently withdraw or move a remote item.

player_benefit: A player can see bounded summaries of distant stock while understanding that the goods remain physical and cannot be withdrawn by magic.
adventure_route: Maps, route notes, or an outpost discovery can establish which distant warehouse is known.
civic_route: Connected settlements can publish read-only stock summaries through registered depots.
mastery_route: Merchant or Cartographer knowledge can improve confidence and freshness labels.
technical_route: A versioned index projection serves bounded read-only requests without scanning every chunk.
economic_route: A steward can quote a real shipment, fare, or lead time rather than offering an instant withdrawal.
dependencies: Warehouse index; route registry; logistics request and reservation records; cross-dimension boundary.
existing_mod_candidate: No safe off-the-shelf candidate verified; storage and logistics adapters are provisional.
custom_integration_required: Yes: read-only projection, stale state, and shipment boundary.
notes: Remote visibility is not a universal warehouse. A later Portal Depot must be explicit physical infrastructure.

player_benefit: Large projects can obtain common stone through several deliberate supply chains instead of an AFK generator being the only sensible preparation.
adventure_route: A quarry region, exposed cliff, or abandoned masonry site supplies the first stock and knowledge.
civic_route: A registered quarry, stoneworks, or settlement demand can produce reliable bulk orders.
mastery_route: Mason or Excavator breadth can improve selective quarrying and reduce wasted handling, not add an infinite multiplier.
technical_route: A generator or processing line may reach high throughput only with real inputs, infrastructure, design, and output handling.
economic_route: A mason, carrier, or warehouse can buy and import stone against a real order.
dependencies: Projects; warehouses; logistics; data-driven demand and storage caps.
existing_mod_candidate: Create-style processing or quarry mod candidate (provisional), not selected for 26.2.
custom_integration_required: Yes: cap passive output, connect demand, and expose the physical supply route.
notes: Vanilla mining remains valid. Any engineered route must compete through investment and handling, not a hidden infinite bonus.

player_benefit: Building, fuel, storage, and transport projects can obtain timber without forcing every player into a high-volume tree farm.
adventure_route: A first forest expedition records species, habitat, and a sustainable source.
civic_route: A managed woodland, forester, or settlement timber yard provides repeatable stock.
mastery_route: Naturalist or Builder breadth can support species-aware harvesting and replanting.
technical_route: A tree system may be engineered for throughput, but it must require space, saplings, time, and output handling.
economic_route: Timber can be commissioned, traded, or moved from a known region through a physical route.
dependencies: Regional knowledge; storage; forestry rules; demand and replanting data.
existing_mod_candidate: Forestry or tree-farm mod candidate TBD (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: regional supply tags, bounded output, and non-destructive replanting rules.
notes: A managed woodland is an infrastructure service, not an infinite passive percentage bonus.

player_benefit: Glassworks, windows, concrete, bottles, and decoration can be supplied without a permanent desert mining chore or an unexamined duplication loop.
adventure_route: The first desert, river, or ruin survey establishes sand knowledge and a regional source.
civic_route: A glassworks, kiln, or mason service turns declared inputs into stock for local projects.
mastery_route: Mason or Glassworker technique can reduce breakage and improve processing choices.
technical_route: A smelting or processing line can scale with sand, fuel, containers, and receiving capacity.
economic_route: Desert imports and glass commissions connect regions through a real warehouse or route.
dependencies: Processing recipes; warehouse; freight; regional resource records.
existing_mod_candidate: Vanilla smelting; Create-style processing candidate (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: supply accounting, output caps, and safe integration with recipe viewers.
notes: Do not remove sand duplication or mining routes before an equally understandable glass supply exists.

player_benefit: A harvest or hunt remains useful across seasons and journeys without forcing constant crop reaping or making spoilage an invisible deletion rule.
adventure_route: A region can reveal a preservation method, ingredient, salt source, cold store, or drying practice.
civic_route: A pantry, smokehouse, cellar, or communal kitchen turns surplus into stable stock.
mastery_route: Cook or Naturalist technique can improve quality, duration, or suitability without requiring a single cuisine.
technical_route: Cooling, drying, smoking, or packing may be automated with real inputs and bounded storage.
economic_route: Preserved food can be bought, commissioned, or imported with known quality and shelf life.
dependencies: Food traits; seasonal or climate adapter; storage; visible quality and expiry rules.
existing_mod_candidate: Serene Seasons and cooking-mod candidates (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: readable preservation state, cross-mod food mapping, and bounded effects.
notes: Ordinary vanilla food remains edible. Preservation extends choice and reduces waste, rather than becoming a mandatory hunger tax.

player_benefit: A discovered regional ingredient becomes renewable at home through a greenhouse, habitat, or cultivation practice.
adventure_route: First access comes from a real regional discovery, sample, or seed exchange.
civic_route: A functional greenhouse, garden, or settlement farm provides a dependable local growing place.
mastery_route: Farmer or Naturalist mastery develops soil, climate, pollination, and harvest technique.
technical_route: Irrigation, climate control, and harvest handling can scale production with energy, water, space, and inputs.
economic_route: Seeds, cuttings, and produce can be traded or imported after the ingredient is known.
dependencies: Regional knowledge; crop data; climate abstraction; greenhouse validation; storage.
existing_mod_candidate: Serene Seasons and farming mods are provisional until 26.2 and trait compatibility are tested.
custom_integration_required: Yes: discovery state, climate abstraction, crop traits, and bounded yield.
notes: Specialisation should make cultivation excellent, not make non-farmers unable to eat ordinary food.

player_benefit: A horse or pack animal can carry useful freight on roads and overland trips without becoming a universal storage or flight system.
adventure_route: Finding and bonding with a suitable animal is a meaningful early exploration route.
civic_route: A stable, paddock, or waystation provides care, loading, and safe hand-off.
mastery_route: Rider or Animal Handler mastery improves handling, load planning, and terrain choices.
technical_route: Cargo harnesses or loading stations can streamline transfer while respecting entity capacity and care.
economic_route: A carrier or stable service can move goods along a registered road for a visible cost.
dependencies: Animal rules; route registration; physical cargo containers; welfare and failure handling.
existing_mod_candidate: Animal and horse-cargo mod candidate TBD (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: cargo identity, capacity, and route/logistics hand-off.
notes: A mount's advantage is contextual. It is not a boat, rail service, warehouse, or vertical flight replacement.

player_benefit: Field travel becomes safer and less interruptive without turning every bedroll into an instant teleport or a risk-free respawn exploit.
adventure_route: An expedition can discover a camp practice and carry a limited bedroll.
civic_route: Inns, camps, and settlements can provide valid rest points and recovery services.
mastery_route: Explorer or Rider technique can improve camp placement and route confidence.
technical_route: Server-authoritative rest and respawn rules validate dimension, danger, ownership, and cooldown state.
economic_route: A traveller can pay for an inn or camp service, while solo use remains viable.
dependencies: Death and respawn policy; route knowledge; bedroll item state; world-save safety.
existing_mod_candidate: Comforts-style bedroll mod candidate (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: safe respawn projection and interaction with journey skipping.
notes: Bedroll convenience must not erase first-trip geography or make death consequences unknowable.

player_benefit: Players can plan work, travel, crops, and expeditions using a forecast that is useful without making weather irrelevant.
adventure_route: Observation of local patterns and landmarks teaches the first forecast signs.
civic_route: A weather station, observatory, or civic calendar publishes a local forecast.
mastery_route: Naturalist or Mariner technique improves forecast confidence and interpretation.
technical_route: Sensors or climate data can produce bounded forecasts without permanent chunk-wide scans.
economic_route: A forecaster or caravan service can sell a route-specific warning or schedule.
dependencies: Climate abstraction; season/weather adapter; local station registration; Field Guide explanation.
existing_mod_candidate: Serene Seasons climate adapter (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: stable forecast vocabulary and safe no-op fallback for absent weather mods.
notes: Forecasts should describe uncertainty and region scope. They are not passive percentage-stat buffs.

player_benefit: A useful path becomes an inspectable, serviceable route for cargo and later journey skipping without making ordinary paths require registration.
adventure_route: A survey expedition records markers, hazards, and a traversed corridor.
civic_route: A settlement or outpost registers a functional connection between named markers.
mastery_route: Cartographer or Builder technique can improve survey quality and route documentation.
technical_route: A bounded corridor check caches validation and invalidates on known changes rather than scanning continuously.
economic_route: A carrier can offer a paid road service with capacity and maintenance terms.
dependencies: Explicit route records; marker identities; bounded validation; settlement graph; world save.
existing_mod_candidate: Vanilla markers plus route integration; transport mod candidate TBD (provisional).
custom_integration_required: Yes: route registry, cached evidence, invalidation, and described failure results.
notes: Registration evaluates function, not architecture. Unregistered vanilla paths remain fully usable.

player_benefit: A validated fixed route can carry people reliably and eventually beat flight for repeated journeys without erasing geography on the first trip.
adventure_route: The player discovers stations and physically travels the line before any skip is available.
civic_route: Stations, platforms, shelter, and settlement connections give the line a civic home.
mastery_route: Engineer or Cartographer mastery improves survey, service planning, and maintenance evidence.
technical_route: Bounded station-to-station graph validation provides service capacity and detects broken links safely.
economic_route: A rail operator can provide fares, schedules, and passenger service without another player being online.
dependencies: Rail graph; station capabilities; route registration; journey-skipping gate; freight boundary.
existing_mod_candidate: Vanilla rail or Create rail candidate (provisional for 26.2).
custom_integration_required: Yes: service validation, fares, route history, and server-authoritative passenger outcomes.
notes: Rail must win on repeated fixed routes through reliability, capacity, or service time, not by disabling walking.

player_benefit: Rivers, coasts, and oceans become useful travel corridors with a service layer for passengers and freight.
adventure_route: A first voyage discovers navigable water, hazards, and a destination port.
civic_route: A port, dock, lighthouse, and warehouse provide a civic connection.
mastery_route: Mariner or Fisher technique improves route reading, loading, and weather decisions.
technical_route: Boat handling, schedules, and bounded route checks can support service without forcing loaded chunks.
economic_route: A shipping service can charge for a real passage or move cargo through receiving buffers.
dependencies: Water continuity; ports; weather; route registry; physical cargo; logistics state machine.
existing_mod_candidate: Small Ships or other boat mods are provisional until 26.2 and server behaviour are verified.
custom_integration_required: Yes: port registration, service records, and freight/passenger hand-off.
notes: Port travel complements rail and roads. It must not be a disguised instant teleport menu.

player_benefit: A deliberately built cross-dimensional depot can move real cargo while preserving dimension boundaries and avoiding a magical universal warehouse.
adventure_route: Exploration discovers and safely traverses the relevant portal pair.
civic_route: A portal depot is a registered civic facility with receiving space and safety rules at both ends.
mastery_route: Logistics or Engineer mastery can document compatible cargo handling and failure recovery.
technical_route: A bounded portal adapter validates both endpoints and transfers physical stacks through durable shipment states.
economic_route: A merchant can quote inter-dimensional freight with capacity, cost, and visible service time.
dependencies: ADR 0012; logistics state machine; portal endpoints; durable cargo; cross-dimension validation.
existing_mod_candidate: No off-the-shelf universal warehouse selected; portal/logistics mod candidates are provisional.
custom_integration_required: Yes: cross-dimension authority, crash recovery, and no magical withdrawal.
notes: This is a specialised infrastructure option. It cannot be a silent shortcut around route construction or storage safety.

player_benefit: Large deliberate construction becomes less repetitive while the player still chooses the design, supplies real materials, and retains normal placement freedom.
adventure_route: A found plan, ruin, or observed technique can teach an optional construction method.
civic_route: A declared civic project gives the assistance a site, purpose, and functional validation.
mastery_route: Builder or Mason mastery can improve technique and repeatable details without making a style mandatory.
technical_route: Server-authoritative batching, bounded shapes, palette replacement, storage reservations, and tool costs make scale safe.
economic_route: A contractor or material supplier can support a project using real stock and a visible work order.
dependencies: Ghost-plan format; project validation; physical inventories; server permissions; equipment condition.
existing_mod_candidate: Effortless Building, Litematica, WorldEdit, and Construction Wand are all provisional candidates. See building-assistance.md.
custom_integration_required: Yes: unify limits, material consumption, authority, accessibility, and project outcomes around existing tools.
notes: Assistance is optional. No structure registration, Builder specialisation, or blueprint may gate ordinary block placement.

player_benefit: A player can preview, inspect, rotate, mirror, and manually build a plan without the plan printing itself into the world.
adventure_route: A plan is discovered, authored, or recovered as knowledge during exploration.
civic_route: A library, workshop, or settlement archive can store and explain plans.
mastery_route: Builder or Mason practice can teach palette substitutions and functional adaptation.
technical_route: A validated importer can bound volume, reject unsafe data, and translate formats without granting creative permissions.
economic_route: A designer can commission a plan or sell a documented pattern while material ownership stays explicit.
dependencies: Schematic parser; ghost rendering; palette categories; project scope; server authority; licence review.
existing_mod_candidate: Litematica/.litematic and WorldEdit/.schem candidates are provisional; exact 26.2 format tests are required.
custom_integration_required: Yes: safe format translation, project identity, and server-side material/cost checks.
notes: A schematic is a plan, not an item printer. Format support must never import hidden entities, unsafe commands, or free materials.

player_benefit: Retain the pivot's named late-world legacy or illumination outcome without making its undefined meaning an accidental progression gate.
adventure_route: Could be a first-discovery narrative or world-history reward once its meaning is specified.
civic_route: Could be a memorial, beacon, or civic legacy outcome once its owner and validation are accepted.
mastery_route: Could record a significant chronicle technique, but must not be a repeat counter.
technical_route: Could use a bounded world-history record, but no implementation contract currently exists.
economic_route: Could be commissioned or patronised if the future design makes it a public legacy rather than a private power.
dependencies: A dedicated specification and ADR are missing; likely world chronicle and exploration dependencies.
existing_mod_candidate: UNKNOWN. No existing project or Matcha candidate is verified.
custom_integration_required: Yes, pending an explicit definition and ticket.
notes: The current repository does not define Last Light. It is deliberately Prestige and cannot gate materials, repair, travel, or ordinary building until a specification resolves the term.

player_benefit: A named, historically important item can be located or reclaimed after loss without creating duplicate copies or deleting unrelated inventory data.
adventure_route: A recovery expedition can follow a last-known location, witness, or physical trail.
civic_route: A home archive, memorial, or settlement registry can preserve recovery information.
mastery_route: Equipment-history evidence identifies why an item matters without rewarding repetitive loss.
technical_route: A durable locator and atomic transaction reconcile item state across death, containers, shipments, and restart.
economic_route: An insurer, courier, or recovery contract can provide a visible service with real limits.
dependencies: Equipment history; world chronicle; death handling; storage and shipment reconciliation.
existing_mod_candidate: No existing candidate verified; custom connective system required.
custom_integration_required: Yes: identity, recovery state, and duplication-safe reconciliation.
notes: Recovery is not a free replacement. If the original cannot be safely identified, the system must surface uncertainty rather than guess.

player_benefit: A mason can produce efficient, precise, and varied structural details without imposing a single architectural theme on every settlement.
adventure_route: A regional ruin, quarry, or mentor can reveal a masonry technique or material relationship.
civic_route: A mason's workshop and a functional building project provide a place to practise and apply it.
mastery_route: Mason mastery rewards breadth across materials, functions, scales, and terrain rather than block-count repetition.
technical_route: Cutting, shaping, and palette tools can scale output while consuming real materials and tool condition.
economic_route: A professional mason can be commissioned to make details or supply prepared components.
dependencies: Builder/Mason mastery; projects; palette substitution; material data; Field Guide.
existing_mod_candidate: Architectural block and masonry mods are provisional; no specific 26.2 candidate is selected.
custom_integration_required: Yes: capability unlocks, guide entries, and functional rather than aesthetic validation.
notes: Advanced does not mean universally best. Vanilla blocks, styles, and manual placement remain first-class.

player_benefit: Villagers and players can develop repeatable skills and institutional knowledge without requiring a trading hall or another human player.
adventure_route: An expedition can find a mentor, school, guild, or regional practice.
civic_route: A school, workplace, workshop, or settlement can host training and preserve taught knowledge.
mastery_route: A player can demonstrate breadth, technique, and project outcomes to qualify for training.
technical_route: Schedules and training queues use bounded abstract simulation when unloaded, with no permanent chunk loading.
economic_route: A trainer can be hired or a course commissioned, with clear price, duration, and outcome.
dependencies: Villager career state; institutional knowledge; settlement/workplace graph; data-driven curricula.
existing_mod_candidate: Villager-career mod candidate TBD (provisional); custom connective layer required.
custom_integration_required: Yes: server-authoritative career records, migration, and bounded simulation.
notes: Training creates repeatability, not passive percentage-stat stacking. Knowledge may outlive a villager only when it was taught.

player_benefit: Repeated trips can eventually become routine enough to skip after the world has physically learned and built the service.
adventure_route: Both endpoints are discovered and the route is physically travelled before skipping is available.
civic_route: A road, rail line, port, or depot is built, registered, maintained, and given a service home.
mastery_route: Cartographer or Steward evidence can explain route confidence and missing proofs.
technical_route: Cached route validation and explicit invalidation prevent continuous world scans and stale teleport permissions.
economic_route: A fare, schedule, or shipment service makes the skip a real route operation rather than a free coordinate jump.
dependencies: ADR 0010; ADR 0018; route graph; endpoint discovery; service validity; world save.
existing_mod_candidate: Rail/route mod candidates are provisional. Waystones-like immediate teleport is not an approved baseline.
custom_integration_required: Yes: proof ledger, service cost, failure reason, and server-authoritative outcome.
notes: Fast travel never creates discoveries, goods, or cross-dimensional access that the player has not physically established.

player_benefit: Knowledge can travel between people and settlements without forcing every player to repeat every expedition or exposing exact artifact coordinates by default.
adventure_route: A charted landmark or route creates the first map fact.
civic_route: Cartographic archives and settlement records can share broad regional knowledge.
mastery_route: Explorer or Cartographer mastery improves confidence, annotation, and interpretation.
technical_route: A bounded map index stores family tags and evidence references rather than scanning the world for all points of interest.
economic_route: A cartographer or merchant can sell a map, rumour, or route lead with visible confidence.
dependencies: Exploration ledger; Field Guide; map data; broad region-family tags; privacy and sharing rules.
existing_mod_candidate: Map and journey mods are provisional; no 26.2 candidate is selected.
custom_integration_required: Yes: stable knowledge concepts and safe sharing without leaking Matcha internals.
notes: Maps should communicate region families and confidence. They are not a linear checklist of exact coordinates.

player_benefit: A remote request moves actual goods through reservations, cargo, routes, buffers, and receiving actions rather than making items appear.
adventure_route: An expedition can establish a source, destination, and usable route.
civic_route: Warehouses, depots, stations, and receiving buffers give freight a physical civic home.
mastery_route: Merchant or Logistics mastery can improve planning and exception handling.
technical_route: A durable, idempotent shipment state machine handles bounded transfers and restart recovery.
economic_route: A carrier or merchant can price capacity, time, and service quality using real inventories.
dependencies: Storage source of truth; logistics state machine; route registration; shipment persistence.
existing_mod_candidate: Storage and logistics mod candidates TBD (provisional); custom connective system required.
custom_integration_required: Yes: reservations, manifests, crash recovery, and duplication resistance.
notes: Freight can be convenient but never magical. Cross-dimension freight requires a separate Portal Depot capability.

player_benefit: Passive systems reduce repetitive waiting while remaining bounded by storage, demand, inputs, and sharply diminishing unattended value.
adventure_route: A discovery can reveal a production possibility or a regional input.
civic_route: A registered works, farm, or settlement demand gives passive output a purpose and receiving capacity.
mastery_route: Producer mastery improves design and adaptation, not an infinitely stacking output multiplier.
technical_route: Engineered production may reach high throughput with real inputs, infrastructure, design, and output handling.
economic_route: A merchant or warehouse can create orders that absorb output, with saturation visible to the player.
dependencies: Farm-pressure policy; storage and demand caps; machine inputs; output handling; metrics.
existing_mod_candidate: Create and other technical production mods are provisional until 26.2 balance is measured.
custom_integration_required: Yes: common cap vocabulary and cross-mod telemetry, not a custom replacement for every machine.
notes: This is a balancing capability, not permission to AFK forever. Engineering is a good route, not the mandatory entrance fee.

player_benefit: A plan can adapt to available or regional materials while preserving function and showing every substitution before placement.
adventure_route: A regional building style or recovered plan can introduce compatible material families.
civic_route: A project declares acceptable primary wall, secondary wall, trim, roof, floor, window, and foundation alternatives.
mastery_route: Builder or Mason technique can judge functional equivalence and record deliberate choices.
technical_route: A server validator resolves substitutions, counts real stacks, and rejects unsafe or ambiguous mappings.
economic_route: A designer or supplier can prepare a palette for a commission without forcing one theme.
dependencies: Schematic parser; palette categories; project validation; material tags; Field Guide.
existing_mod_candidate: Effortless Building, Litematica, and WorldEdit are provisional candidates for different layers.
custom_integration_required: Yes: category semantics, previews, costs, and server validation.
notes: No architecture style is mandatory. Palette categories describe function, not a prescribed appearance.

player_benefit: Cooks and alchemists can make regional ingredients understandable and useful without opaque recipe puzzles or unlimited effect stacking.
adventure_route: Discovering an ingredient or preparation reveals its traits and a documented process.
civic_route: A kitchen, pantry, or communal meal makes knowledge useful to a settlement.
mastery_route: Cook or Herbalist mastery develops combinations and safe technique through breadth and projects.
technical_route: A recipe system exposes bounded duration, intensity, conflicts, and contraindications.
economic_route: A cook, apothecary, or merchant can sell prepared food with readable properties.
dependencies: Food trait vocabulary; Field Guide; recipe viewer; climate and ingredient adapters.
existing_mod_candidate: Cooking and alchemy mods are provisional; no 26.2 candidate is selected.
custom_integration_required: Yes: stable trait mapping and bounded effect outcomes.
notes: Traits are named functions, not generic rarity tiers or passive percentage trinkets. Ordinary vanilla food remains useful.

player_benefit: A building or remote outpost can become a recognised functional node for storage, routes, rest, or services without requiring a theme or a circular claim area.
adventure_route: An expedition can establish a remote outpost at a meaningful landmark.
civic_route: A settlement registers buildings, work sites, storage, and connections as a graph.
mastery_route: Builder or Steward projects can demonstrate function and maintain the record.
technical_route: Bounded validation checks only declared capabilities and caches the result.
economic_route: A steward can charter, supply, or insure an outpost through visible costs and permissions.
dependencies: Settlement graph; registered buildings; route markers; storage and service capabilities.
existing_mod_candidate: No existing candidate verified; custom connective system required.
custom_integration_required: Yes: graph records, validation, persistence, and safe invalidation.
notes: Registration adds services. It never becomes a prerequisite for ordinary block placement or basic survival.
